newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF nominee Guillen says not anti-Maastricht.
newsitem.headline: BoF nominee Guillen says not anti-Maastricht.

text.p: Pierre Guillen, one of six candidates to fill a vacancy on the Bank of France's monetary policy council, said on Wednesday he was not against a single currency and was "radically against" devaluing the franc.
"I am neither anti-Maastricht nor against a single currency," Guillen told Reuters in an interview.

Afternoon daily Le Monde said President Jacques Chirac had wanted Guillen, described by newspapers as against moves to monetary union and France's "franc fort", on the list of six candidates to fill two posts coming up in early January.

"I voted for the Maastricht treaty, you can check, and I always, in the employers' association, argued for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and I spoke without ambiguity on Monday at the executive council (of the employers' association CNPF) in favour of the current parity of the currency," he said.

Guillen, who stepped down as vice-president of the CNPF on Tuesday, and remains honorary president of the union of metallurgical and mining industries, was reported by French newspaper Liberation to be an opponent of the strong franc policy.
Political observers have speculated that Chirac could use the expiry of the terms of two members of the council to tilt the balance of power at the Bank more in favour of a softer monetary policy.
Guillen refused to give an opinion on whether the Bank of France should cut rates sharply in order to boost the economy.
"How could I know if it should be 40, (basis points) 50, or 10," he said. "I refuse to comment on these matters as long as I have not spent several days on the monetary policy council."

"I am not in favour of devaluation," he said. "Now there are a certain number of adjustments on which I might be able to comment. But I would have to look personally at the matters and no one has given me the elements."

"Like many industrialists, I wanted interest rates to come down a little bit faster, but that's an opinion that is an opinion of a representative of industry and that's it. I am not the only one to offer that view."
